events.title: The Broken Grain Sifter
events.prose: Elias spent three days hunched over the heavy iron sifter. He left a handful of replacement gears on Ruth's doorstep without a note, though he wouldn't admit to the repair.

events.title: A Quiet Shared Joke
events.prose: Silas leaned across the counter to whisper something that made Ruth's shoulders shake with laughter. The laughter died quickly, leaving a heavy silence that neither of them knew how to break.

events.title: Unclaimed Winter Correspondence
events.prose: Mabel sorted through a stack of undelivered letters and found one addressed to Ruth's late father. She tucked it into her apron pocket, intending to find the right moment to mention it.

events.title: Storm Clouds Over Cicada
events.prose: Caleb attempted to fix the boardwalk railing as the sky turned a bruised purple. He looked at Ruth as she walked past, his mouth opening as if to say something important, before he simply went back to his hammer.

memories.text: Elias spent three days hunched over the heavy iron sifter until the gears finally meshed.
He left a small pile of replacement parts on Ruth's doorstep in the early morning light.
He avoided looking at Ruth when she thanked the wind for the sudden repair.
Silas leaned across the diner counter to whisper a joke that made Ruth shake with laughter.
He felt the weight of the sudden silence that followed their shared moment.
He owed Ruth a real explanation for why he couldn't look her in the eye after the laughter died.
Mabel watched Ruth pause for a long second in front of the post office window.
She tucked a yellowed letter addressed to Ruth's father deep into her apron pocket.
She left a small basket of rosemary bread on the doorstep of the woman who had lost her husband.
Caleb watched Ruth mend her apron by the light of a single lamp.
He carried a heavy crate of cider from the mill to the Rusty Spoke.
He owed Silas three silver coins from their last poker game.
